newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Taxes may halve Russian oil output soon - executive.
newsitem.headline: Taxes may halve Russian oil output soon - executive.

text.p: Russian crude oil output could plummet by up to 50 percent by 2000 if existing taxes are not lowered, a senior Russian industry executive said on Tuesday.

"(Total Russian) output, under the current taxes that we have, could fall to 150-170 million tonnes (3.0-3.4 million barrels per day, or bpd) by 2000," Pavel Fyodorov, vice president for economic issues at mini-major Sibneft, told an energy conference.
Total Russian oil output in 1996 was 6.03 million bpd, down 47 percent from a 1987 peak of 11.39 million barrels per day.

Russia, once the world's biggest oil producer, has seen its output decline steadily over 10 or so years, but the world's third largest oil producer is showing signs of closing the gap on steep declines.
But Fyodorov said that excise tariffs on produced oil did not differentiate geological and geographical factors that make output in certain areas more expensive.
From 40 percent to 70 percent of all Russian oil produced, depending on the company and its location, was in high-cost, hard-to-recover areas, he said.
Russian oil producers pay an average excise output rate of 55,000 roubles per tonne. "This is also a high figure and is not enabling us to raise output," Fyodorov said.

But he said that oil companies were finding a sympathetic ear in both the government and the Fuel and Energy Ministry, and that a new Tax Code, still to be passed, would probably have special rates for hydrocarbons producers.
Sibneft owns Russia's largest oil refinery, Omsk. Its production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz.
